article.title: Infinitivo flexionado: equivalencias parciales entre portugués y español
article.part: Contraste Guatemala–Brasil y dominio avanzado C1–C2 — Contraste Guatemala–Brasil e domínio avançado C1–C2
article.chapter: Contraste español de Guatemala–portugués de Brasil — Contraste espanhol da Guatemala–português do Brasil

claims.summary: The contrastive study describes the Portuguese personal/inflected infinitive as capable of carrying person marking and an overt subject.
The article gives depois de virem / después de venir ellos and compares via os rosarios das oliveiras riscarem colinas with its Spanish translation veía los rosarios de olivos rayar las colinas.

The authors examine 246 selected personal infinitives from Memorial do convento and its Spanish translation, exclude ambiguous and some low-frequency cases, and find infinitives often correspond but no full equivalence across all syntactic, semantic and pragmatic values.
The study supports Spanish infinitives as frequent equivalents in the dependent clauses analyzed, while showing that equivalence varies by context and is not complete.
